tasks.title: Blog Post #2: Docling vs Marker (Traditional ML Beats VLM)
tasks.description: Write attention-grabbing post on surprising finding: IBM's traditional CV/ML parser (Docling) beats VLM-based parser (Marker) on structure
tasks.parallel_opportunities: Can write in parallel with TASK-004, TASK-006
acceptance_criteria: 2,000-2,500 words with clear data comparison
Head-to-head metrics table: Docling vs Marker across all dimensions
Explanation of why traditional ML won (document structure is a solved CV problem)
Discussion of VLM advantages (text recognition, unclear layouts)
Balanced perspective: not 'VLMs are bad' but 'traditional ML still competitive'
Attention-grabbing headline for HN/Reddit
structure: 1. Hook: 'VLMs are the future' narrative challenged
2. The Matchup: Docling (IBM, open-source, traditional) vs Marker+Ollama (VLM)
3. Results: Docling wins element_f1 (84.1% vs 69.4%), tree_sim (61.2% vs 49.3%)
4. Why Traditional ML Won: Document structure is geometric, not semantic
5. Where VLMs Excel: Text recognition (89.9% vs 87.4%)
6. Trade-offs: Speed (docling 3× faster), reliability (marker 7% better)
7. Implications: Don't assume VLMs beat everything; test on your domain
8. Conclusion: Hybrid approaches may be optimal

tasks.title: Blog Post #3: The 50% Structure Preservation Gap
tasks.description: Write post on industry-wide problem: all parsers achieve 83% text accuracy but only 33% structure preservation
tasks.parallel_opportunities: Can write in parallel with TASK-004, TASK-005
acceptance_criteria: 2,000-2,500 words explaining the structure problem
Data from all 10 parsers showing consistent gap
Concrete examples: heading hierarchy lost, list nesting flattened
Impact analysis: why this matters for RAG, LLM context, search
Discussion of why this is hard (PDF has no semantic structure)
Call to action: prioritize structure metrics, not just text accuracy
structure: 1. The Problem: 'My parser has 90% accuracy' is misleading
2. The Data: All 10 parsers show 50-point structure gap
3. What Gets Lost: Heading levels, list nesting, section hierarchy, reading order
4. Real-World Impact: RAG chunks lose context, LLMs miss document structure
5. Why This Is Hard: PDF stores coordinates, not semantics
6. Case Studies: Multi-column layouts, nested lists, complex tables
7. What Success Looks Like: Docling at 61.2% is still failing 40% of structure
8. Recommendations: Measure structure, choose parsers accordingly, hybrid strategies
